commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: artifact-design
commands.description: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.

commands.name: artifact-diagramming
commands.description: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.

commands.name: artifact-capabilities
commands.description: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug

commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. commands.name: simplify

commands.name: batch

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts

commands.name: doctor

commands.name: loop

commands.name: claude-api

## What was actually wrong

The file had drifted away from three contracts it depends on. Each error was fixed by conforming to the real type, not by weakening it:

**1. `BusinessTruth` (TS2305, TS2554)** — no such type exists. `getBusinessTruthContext()` is synchronous, takes no arguments, and returns `string` — exactly what `RemediationInput.truthContext` wants. Removed the phantom import and the bogus `await …(customerId) as BusinessTruth`.

**2. Drizzle schema mismatches (TS2769, TS2322, TS2353, TS2339)**
- `discovery_runs.startedAt/completedAt` are `bigint({mode:'number'})` epoch-millis, not `timestamp` — passing `Date` objects was wrong.
- `sweep_triggers` has no `sweepId`, `triggeredAt`, `evaluation`, or `result` columns; it has a `serial` `id` plus required `reasons` and `affectedSurfaces`. The insert now writes the real columns and reads the DB-assigned id back via `.returning({ id })` — which is also the `number` that `SweepResult.sweepId` and `remediation_actions.sweepId` expect.
- Surface statuses are `discovered | reviewed | stale | dead | ignored`; the query filtered on a non-existent `'new'`. Now uses the `DiscoveryStatus` enum that was already imported but unused.

**3. `SweepResult` / `SweepEvaluation` shape (TS2339, TS7006)** — the code invented `{status, surfacesProcessed, errors}` and an array of surface ids. The declared types (used by `server/cron/cron-router.ts`) are `{sweepId, surfacesReviewed, surfacesRemediated, issuesFound, durationMs}` and `affectedSurfaces: number`. The implementation now returns those; sweep status/errors go to the DB row and the log where they belong. `evaluateForSweep` was also calling `.select()` on an un-awaited `getDb()` promise.

**4. The remediation call (TS2454, TS2488, TS2739)** — `shieldResults.map(...)` read the variable before it was assigned, and `gatedRemediateSweepResults` was called with one argument instead of its real `(sweepId, customerId, surfaceResults, truthContext, config?)` signature, with a return type annotated from the wrong function. The gate needs a per-surface `reviewResult`, which nothing produced. I filled that gap the way the module's own design implies — the previously-dead `mapSurfaceTypeToShieldType` helper existed for exactly this — by reviewing each surface's snapshot through `shieldReviewContent` (dynamic import, matching `gravito-gate.ts`'s circular-dependency pattern) and feeding only surfaces with findings into the gate. The helper's return type is now the Shield `SurfaceType` union rather than `string`, so no cast is needed at the call site.

One thing worth flagging: this also removed a pre-existing error at `server/cron/cron-router.ts:1233`, which passed `'coverage_drop'` to a parameter typed `'manual' | 'scheduled'`. The declared `SweepTriggerType` in `types.ts` includes `'coverage_drop'`, so widening the parameter to that type was the correct fix rather than narrowing the caller.

I did not touch `server/governance/surface-discovery/webhook-adapter.ts:19`, which imports a non-existent `ProactiveCoherencePipelineResult` from this file. Exporting that name would resolve its import error but surface three new ones (`coverageReport`, `remediationResults` don't exist on the pipeline result), which the current error masks — a net-new-error trade the task rules forbid. That file's errors are unchanged from baseline.

The insert now writes the real columns and reads the DB-assigned id back via `.returning({ id })` — which is also the `number` that `SweepResult.sweepId` and `remediation_actions.sweepId` expect.
- Surface statuses are `discovered | reviewed | stale | dead | ignored`; the query filtered on a non-existent `'new'`. Now uses the `DiscoveryStatus` enum that was already imported but unused.

**3. `SweepResult` / `SweepEvaluation` shape (TS2339, TS7006)** — the code invented `{status, surfacesProcessed, errors}` and an array of surface ids. The declared types (used by `server/cron/cron-router.ts`) are `{sweepId, surfacesReviewed, surfacesRemediated, issuesFound, durationMs}` and `affectedSurfaces: number`. The implementation now returns those; sweep status/errors go to the DB row and the log where they belong. `evaluateForSweep` was also calling `.select()` on an un-awaited `getDb()` promise.
